title: Visual Project Map
description: A browser-based tool that visualizes project workflows as interactive DAGs. Accepts three inputs: (A) scan an existing project directory, (B) design a workflow from a natural language objective, (C) render existing graph JSON. The schema and inference rules define what generators produce; the generation skills create graph JSON; the viewer renders it with collapsible modules, interface ports, confidence flags, and progressive disclosure.
_objective: Build a browser-based tool that visualizes project workflows as interactive DAGs. It accepts three inputs: (A) scan an existing project directory to infer workflow structure, (B) design a workflow from a natural language objective before any code exists, (C) render an existing graph JSON. The viewer shows collapsible module groups with interface ports, confidence/checkpoint flags, and progressive disclosure from big-picture to detail. Output is a JSON file conforming to a schema, plus an interactive browser viewer built on Cytoscape.js with dagre layout.

modules.label: Schema & Rules
modules.description: Define the graph data model and the heuristic rules that drive generation. The schema is the contract between generators and the viewer; the rules encode domain knowledge for detecting modules, nodes, edges, confidence, and visual encoding.

modules.label: Schema Definition
modules.description: JSON Schema defining the graph structure: required fields (title, modules, nodes, edges), optional fields (legend, plan, confidence, generation metadata), and all validation constraints.

inputs.name: design_decisions
inputs.description: Architectural decisions about what the graph must represent

outputs.name: schema_json
outputs.description: JSON Schema file that validators and generators reference

outputs.name: graph_schema_doc
outputs.description: Human-readable quick reference for all fields

modules.label: Inference Engine
modules.checkpointReason: Inference rules encode domain-specific heuristics for detecting modules, assigning roles, and assessing confidence — these require iterative refinement against real projects to avoid false positives
modules.description: Lookup tables and heuristics for detecting modules, nodes, edges, shapes, actors, confidence levels, and status from project structure and documentation.

inputs.name: schema_json
inputs.description: Schema defining valid field values and enums

outputs.name: inference_rules
outputs.description: Lookup tables for module detection, role assignment, status inference, confidence heuristics, and design-mode defaults

outputs.name: color_palette
outputs.description: Color assignments for modules, phases, and terminals

modules.label: Generation
modules.description: AI skills that produce graph JSON from different inputs: scanning an existing codebase (Input A), designing from a natural language objective (Input B), or updating an existing graph incrementally.

modules.label: Project Scanner (Input A)
modules.checkpointReason: Scanner quality depends on project conventions — projects without CLAUDE.md or clear folder structure produce sparser graphs; heuristics need tuning against diverse real-world codebases
modules.description: Scan a project directory to infer workflow structure. Reads CLAUDE.md, README, folder structure, script I/O patterns, Makefiles, and CI configs to build a mental model, then feeds it to the assembler.

inputs.name: project_directory
inputs.description: Filesystem path to the project to analyze

outputs.name: discovery_model
outputs.description: Structured mental model: candidate modules, nodes, edges, I/O patterns, actor assignments

modules.label: Workflow Designer (Input B)
modules.checkpointReason: Designing a workflow from a natural language objective is the hardest capability — the AI must decompose ambiguous goals into concrete stages, assess its own confidence, and flag where domain expertise is needed, all without any codebase to ground it
modules.description: Design a complete workflow from a natural language objective. Parses the goal, decomposes into stages using domain knowledge, defines data flow and interfaces, assesses confidence per stage, and feeds the result to the assembler.

inputs.name: objective_text
inputs.description: Natural language description of the goal

outputs.name: design_model
outputs.description: Structured model: phases, modules with interfaces and confidence, nodes, edges with actor assignments

modules.label: Assembly & Output
modules.description: Shared assembly logic for both Input A and Input B. Constructs the graph JSON, enforces the 1-edge-per-module-pair rule, validates references, writes the file, and launches the viewer.

inputs.name: generation_model
inputs.description: Discovery model (Input A) or design model (Input B)

outputs.name: graph_json
outputs.description: Complete graph JSON file ready for the viewer
outputs.format: JSON conforming to schema.json, written to .graphs/{name}.json

modules.label: Viewer
modules.description: Browser-based interactive viewer that renders graph JSON as a collapsible DAG with multiple view modes, progressive disclosure, and rich interactions.

modules.label: Core Renderer
modules.description: Initialize Cytoscape.js, load graph JSON, convert modules/nodes/edges to Cytoscape elements with styles, run dagre layout, and render the initial collapsed view.

inputs.name: graph_json
inputs.description: Graph JSON file loaded via URL parameter

outputs.name: cy_instance
outputs.description: Initialized Cytoscape instance with all elements, styles, and layout applied

modules.label: Collapse Engine
modules.checkpointReason: Custom collapse/expand implementation using cy.remove()/cy.add() has subtle edge cases: meta-edge deduplication across hierarchy levels, preserving user state during toggle, and correct depth-first collapse ordering
modules.description: Handle module collapse and expand by removing/restoring child elements. Build deduplicated meta-edges for cross-module connections when modules are collapsed. Support 2-level nesting (phases containing modules).

outputs.name: collapse_manager
outputs.description: CollapseManager instance that tracks collapsed state and manages meta-edges

modules.label: Interaction Layer
modules.description: User interactions: click-to-toggle on modules, hover highlighting and tooltips, node detail side panel, edge detail modal, search by label, path tracing (upstream/downstream BFS), keyboard shortcuts (F/E/C/L/V/W/M), breadcrumb navigation.

outputs.name: interactive_viewer
outputs.description: Fully interactive graph with all event handlers, panels, and keyboard shortcuts bound

modules.label: View Modes
modules.checkpointReason: Multiple visual encodings (color, border, opacity, glow, shape) must coexist without conflicts — adding a new view mode requires checking it against all existing modes and properties P2.1-P2.13
modules.description: Mutually exclusive view modes that recolor the graph: Module (default), Provenance (trust-state), Actor (edge colors), Files (I/O paths), Plan (overlay glow), Diff (structural comparison), and future Confidence mode. Legend updates per active view.

inputs.name: interactive_viewer
inputs.description: Viewer with all elements and interactions

inputs.name: graph_json
inputs.description: Original graph data for view-specific styling

outputs.name: styled_viewer
outputs.description: Viewer with active view mode applied, correct legend, and V-key cycling

modules.label: Distribution
modules.description: Package the tool as a Claude Code plugin and provide serving infrastructure for local development.

modules.label: Serving & Deployment
modules.description: HTTP server that copies graph JSON into the viewer's examples directory and serves the viewer with the correct relative URL. Plugin manifests for Claude Code marketplace distribution.

inputs.name: graph_json
inputs.description: Graph JSON file at an absolute path

inputs.name: viewer_files
inputs.description: HTML, JS, and CSS files for the viewer

outputs.name: running_server
outputs.description: Local HTTP server with viewer accessible at localhost:PORT

nodes.label: schema.define_fields
nodes.description: Define all required and optional fields: title, modules, nodes, edges, legend, plan, confidence, generation metadata.

nodes.label: schema.add_validation
nodes.description: Add validation constraints: enum values, pattern matching, required arrays, cross-references between module/node/edge IDs.

nodes.label: schema.document
nodes.description: Generate human-readable quick reference (graph-schema.md) with field tables, visual encoding summaries, and examples.

nodes.label: rules.detection_tables
nodes.description: Define lookup tables for module detection (from folders, packages, docs), node shape assignment (from text signals), and edge style/actor assignment.

nodes.label: rules.confidence_heuristics
nodes.description: Define confidence assessment tables for design mode: standard patterns (high) vs domain-specific stages (low, needs review).

nodes.label: rules.design_mode_defaults
nodes.description: Define default field values for Input B graphs: all planned, omit files/trust/details, require interfaces and descriptions.

nodes.label: scan.discover_structure
nodes.description: Glob for docs, scripts, data dirs. Read CLAUDE.md and README. Extract workflow sections, decision language, actor signals.

nodes.label: scan.detect_io_patterns
nodes.description: Grep key scripts for file I/O patterns (read_csv, json.dump, subprocess). Map script inputs to outputs to infer edges.

nodes.label: scan.synthesize_model
nodes.description: Combine folder structure, script groupings, data directories, and documentation into a structured model of phases, modules, and data flow.

nodes.label: scan.diff_existing
nodes.description: If a graph already exists, diff the fresh scan against it: keep unchanged elements, add new ones, flag removals for user confirmation.

nodes.label: design.parse_objective
nodes.description: Extract domain, final deliverable, key entities, constraints, scale signals, and decision/human/AI language from the objective text.

nodes.label: design.decompose_stages
nodes.description: Decompose the objective into sequential workflow stages using domain knowledge. Identify phases, modules, and data flow between them.

nodes.label: design.define_interfaces
nodes.description: For each module pair, identify the intermediate artifact: name, format, quality checks. Produces module.interface fields.

nodes.label: design.assess_confidence
nodes.description: Self-assess each stage: standard (high confidence) vs domain-specific (low, needsHumanReview). Assign checkpointReason where flagged.

nodes.label: assemble.construct_json
nodes.description: Build the complete JSON object from the generation model: modules with colors and interfaces, nodes with shapes and IDs, edges with styles and actors.

nodes.label: assemble.validate_and_enforce
nodes.description: Validate reference integrity, enforce 1-edge-per-module-pair rule, check scope limits, verify all required fields present.

nodes.label: assemble.write_and_serve
nodes.description: Write graph JSON to .graphs/{name}.json, launch the viewer via serve.py, open in browser.

nodes.label: render.init_cytoscape
nodes.description: Create Cytoscape instance, configure dagre layout parameters, set zoom bounds and pan constraints.

nodes.label: render.build_elements
nodes.description: Convert JSON modules to compound nodes, child nodes with shapes/colors/status, and edges with styles/actors. Apply trust, role, and status visual encoding.

nodes.label: render.run_layout
nodes.description: Run dagre hierarchical layout (longest-path ranker, fallback to network-simplex). Collapse all modules and fit to viewport.

nodes.label: collapse.remove_children
nodes.description: On collapse: remove child nodes/edges via cy.remove(), store originals, apply collapsed module style with fixed size and label.

nodes.label: collapse.build_meta_edges
nodes.description: Rebuild deduplicated meta-edges from stored originalEdges. Combine labels, propagate dominant actor color. Handle 2-level nesting.

nodes.label: collapse.restore_children
nodes.description: On expand: re-add stored children via cy.add(), remove meta-edges, re-run layout within the expanded module.

nodes.label: interact.bind_events
nodes.description: Bind click (toggle/detail), hover (highlight/tooltip), double-click (path trace), keyboard shortcuts, toolbar buttons.

nodes.label: interact.detail_panels
nodes.description: Node side panel (description, I/O, files, docs), edge modal (script, input, output), plan summary panel.

nodes.label: interact.navigation
nodes.description: Search by label, path tracing (BFS upstream/downstream), breadcrumb trail, minimap, pan/zoom.

nodes.label: views.mode_switcher
nodes.description: V-key cycling and toolbar buttons to switch between Module, Provenance, Actor, Files, Plan, and Diff views. Each view applies distinct color/style rules.

nodes.label: views.update_legend
nodes.description: Rebuild legend content per active view: module swatches, trust tags, actor colors, file indicators, plan status, or diff summary.

nodes.label: serve.plugin_manifest
nodes.description: Define plugin.json and marketplace.json for Claude Code plugin distribution. Version sync between both files.

nodes.label: serve.http_server
nodes.description: Python HTTP server that copies graph JSON into viewer/examples/, serves static files, and opens the browser with the correct ?graph= URL.

edges.label: inform rules
edges.description: Schema field definitions inform the inference rules — rules must produce values that conform to schema enums and constraints.

edges.label: guide scanning
edges.description: Inference rules provide the lookup tables that the scanner uses to detect modules, assign shapes, and determine actors.

edges.label: assemble
edges.description: Pass the discovery model (new or incrementally updated) to the shared assembly module for JSON construction.

edges.label: guide design
edges.description: Design-mode defaults and confidence heuristics guide how the designer assesses each stage and what fields to include or omit.

edges.label: assemble
edges.description: Pass the design model (all planned, with confidence and interfaces) to the shared assembly module.

edges.label: load JSON
edges.description: The written graph JSON file is loaded by the viewer via HTTP. The serve script handles URL routing.

edges.label: collapse all
edges.description: After initial layout, collapse all modules to show the interface map (big-picture view) by default.

edges.label: bind interactions
edges.description: Once the initial collapsed view is ready, bind all user interaction handlers to the Cytoscape instance.

edges.label: view modes
edges.description: Navigation features (search, path trace, breadcrumbs) are available in all view modes; view switching overlays additional color encoding.

edges.label: serve
edges.description: The assembly module triggers the serve script which starts an HTTP server and opens the viewer in the browser.
